releases.title: Plans now work for sites that were hard to read
releases.summary: Some websites, especially apps that redirect while loading, made the analysis fail after a long wait. To One now reads those pages another way, and tells you plainly when a site can't be reached.

releases.title: MuseumHop opens faster on your first visit
releases.summary: New visitors no longer take a detour through the old MuseumHopper address before the planner loads. Links to the old address still bring you here with your nights and name.

releases.title: Open any release to see what changed
releases.summary: Each row in the shipping log now opens to show what the release does, how to use it, and a link straight to the change on its site.

releases.title: A guided first visit, and help on every page
releases.summary: First-time readers get a three-step intro. A new ? button opens help with a short tour of the page you are on.
how: Tap the ? in the header, or press ? on a keyboard.
Pick “Tour this page” to see what each part does.
Use “Replay the intro” to see the welcome again.

releases.title: The $72.4B line in Anthropic’s accounts, explained
releases.summary: Story 4c of the Anthropic deep dive now answers seven short questions about one accounting line, each linked to its page in the prospectus.
how: Open Deep dive and pick Anthropic.
Scroll to story 4, “One accounting line”.

releases.title: Every page now ends with a sunset and three doors
releases.summary: A reader said reaching the end of Hope felt like the good news had run out. Each page now ends calmly, with three places to go next.
how: Scroll to the bottom of Today, Past & Present or Hopeful Past.
Pick a door: tomorrow’s newsletter, another page, or a friend site.

releases.title: Hopeful Past, retold as a single day
releases.summary: Two centuries of progress squeezed into one day: 1820 is midnight and today is 23:59, about 8.6 years per hour.
how: Open Hopeful Past.
Tap a pin on the day clock to jump to that moment.
Open a decade below to see every event in it, with sources.

releases.title: A coach that tells you why a move is smart
releases.summary: Built on a friend’s feedback: Go Dojo now explains good and bad moves with six truths and twelve rules of thumb, adds smart-move drills, and is easier on a phone.
how: Play a game and tap Coach after any move.
Try the smart-move drills from the Lessons page.

releases.title: SpaceX deep dive, with numbers that update themselves
releases.summary: SpaceX’s prospectus and its last two quarterly reports, told as 11 scrolling stories. The headline numbers refresh daily from SEC filings.
how: Open Deep dive and tap the SpaceX chip.
When a newer filing appears, the page links to it.

releases.title: A three-step intro and a new help panel
releases.summary: New visitors learn the question, the five-layer stack and how to read a bubble in three steps. Companies, Forecasts and Summary moved to the new design.
how: Press ? or tap the ? button.
Choose “What can I do?” for every feature and shortcut.

releases.title: Deep dive: Anthropic’s IPO prospectus
releases.summary: A new Deep dive tab tells the S-1 as eleven stories. One chart stays on screen and highlights each point as you scroll.
how: Open the Deep dive tab.
Scroll. The chart follows and lights up the part being discussed.

releases.title: New overview: the AI layer cake, in bubbles
releases.summary: The homepage is a new overview with year and quarter filters, a play-through timeline, period comparison and a source on every number.
how: Use the sidebar to switch year or quarter.
Press play to watch the bubbles move over time.
Click any bubble for its sources.

releases.title: Newsletter sign-up you can trust
releases.summary: Subscribing now asks you to confirm by email, unsubscribing deletes your address, and a new privacy page says exactly what is stored.
how: Sign up at the bottom of any page.
Click the link in the confirmation email.

releases.title: Pick your mood: the new Today page
releases.summary: Hope now opens on a Today page where you choose the kind of good news you want, plus a new Past & Present page that sets stories next to long-run data.
how: Choose a mood: Surprise me, Warm my heart, Blow my mind or Show me what works.
Use Refine to search or filter by place.
Open Past & Present to see a story beside its Our World in Data chart.

releases.title: Quoth is free for every Mac
releases.summary: One download, no Homebrew: transcription engines ship inside the app, the right model downloads on first run, and updates install themselves.
how: Download the DMG from arian-shafa.xyz/quoth.
The setup page suggests a model for your Mac’s memory.
Use Email the Developer in the menu bar to send feedback.
